title: Roles in Web3, Explained

cards.aki: You do not have to be a coder to work in web3.
cards.title: Roles in Web3, Explained
text: A web3 team looks a lot like any startup: people who build, people who grow, and people who keep it running.
A few jobs are new, because the code holds real money and the community often owns part of the project. Let's meet them, then find where you fit.

cards.aki: Tap each card. These people write the product.
cards.title: Builders

items.back: Writes the code that runs on the blockchain, often in Solidity or Rust. That code can hold millions, so mistakes are costly and careful testing is the job.
Builds the app people actually click: connecting wallets, showing balances and making transactions clear.
Works on the chain itself or what it runs on: nodes, clients, speed and reliability.
Reviews smart contracts for bugs before and after launch. Many projects also pay outside researchers through bug bounties.

cards.aki: No code needed for most of these.
cards.title: Growers

items.back: Runs the Discord or Telegram, answers questions, welcomes newcomers and keeps scammers out.
Helps other builders use the product: docs, tutorials, workshops and hackathons.
Threads, videos, newsletters and memes that explain the product and keep people talking.
Finds partners, integrations and listings, and tracks what actually brings users in.

cards.aki: Every team also needs people who keep it running.
cards.title: Operators

items.back: Decides what to build next and why, by talking to users and turning their problems into plans.
Makes wallets, swaps and sign-in screens simple. Good design in web3 prevents expensive mistakes.
Pays people (sometimes in stablecoins), manages the treasury and keeps the accounts.
Follows the rules in each country: tokens, licences, tax and what the project can and cannot promise.

cards.aki: These roles are more web3 than anywhere else.
cards.title: Research, data and governance
points: Researchers and analysts study projects, markets and onchain data, often building public dashboards.
Tokenomics designers plan who gets the tokens, when they unlock and why.
Governance or DAO coordinators help token holders discuss and vote on decisions, then make sure the results happen.

cards.title: A team is about to launch smart contracts that will hold users' money. Who should check the code for bugs first?

options.why: Yes. An audit, plus a bug bounty, is the usual way to catch costly mistakes before launch.
Community managers talk to users. Reviewing contract code is a security job.
The blockchain runs whatever code it is given, bugs included.

cards.aki: Here is how to find your fit.
cards.title: From where you are to a web3 role

steps.label: 1. Start from your skills
steps.text: Writing, design, code, support, sales, numbers: almost every skill has a web3 version.

steps.label: 2. Pick a role family
steps.text: Builders, growers, operators or research. Choose the one that matches what you already enjoy.

steps.label: 3. Learn the web3 basics
steps.text: Wallets, gas fees, tokens and scams. Enough to talk to users and teammates with confidence.

steps.label: 4. Do public work
steps.text: Write a guide, answer questions in a community, fix a doc, join a hackathon or a bounty.

steps.label: 5. Apply with proof
steps.text: Send links to what you did. In web3, a public piece of work often matters more than a CV.

cards.aki: Some 'jobs' are traps. Know the signs.
cards.title: Red flags in web3 job offers
points: You are asked to pay to apply, for training, or to 'activate' your account.
A recruiter you never met asks you to download and run a file or a test project. Fake job offers have been used to steal crypto.
You would be paid only in the project's own brand-new token.
The 'job' is to promote a token's price or recruit other people.
cards.tip: Check the company's official site and socials, and never run unknown files on a computer that holds your crypto.

cards.title: You love explaining things and helping people in group chats. Which role fits best to start?

options.why: Yes. Helping people in the community every day is exactly the job, and it is a common first role in web3.
That role works deep in the chain's code. Your strength is people.
That needs legal training. Your strength is helping people.

cards.aki: There is a seat for you. Go find it.
cards.title: Quick recap
points: Builders write the code: smart contracts, apps, the chain, and security.
Growers bring people in: community, DevRel, content and partnerships.
Operators keep it running: product, design, finance and legal.
Research and governance are extra web3 roles.
Show public work, and never pay to get a job.
